In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best performing BioNER model is a BiLSTM-CNN-CRF that uses variational dropout, multi-task learning and transfer learning.
the use of deep learning in BioNER has led to a significant increase in in-corpus performance but has not led to an increase in out-of-corpus (generalization) performance.
our work demonstrates the importance of generalization for biomedical NLP and shows that it is possible to improve out-of-corpus BioNER performance by up to 10%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of the best BioNER model is still not as high as the performance reported in the literature.
the performance of a BioNER model trained and tested on the same data is not indicative of the model’s out-of-corpus generalization.
we present a new BioNER tool, Saber, which outperforms the state of the art in both in-corpus and out-of-corpus BioNER performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BioNER is not as robust as it seems, with a significant performance drop when trained on one corpus and evaluated on another.
the generalization ability of deep learning models can be significantly improved for BioNER by using regularization, transfer learning and/or multi-task learning.
the BioNER models that have achieved the best performance to date are not necessarily the ones that generalize well.
